newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge rises on broker upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge rises on broker upgrades.

text.p: Shares in French building materials company Lafarge climbed around four percent on Thursday as brokers upgraded recommendations and forecasts, market sources said.
Lafarge traded up 3.87 percent to 386.4 francs, on volume of 349,397 shares.
The upgrades follow Wednesday's publication of 1996 results, which included higher-than-expected operating profits, and a company presentation which expressed confidence for 1997.
"The company had a very positive message," said an equities desk head.
Market sources said James Capel upgraded the stock to buy from neutral.
CDC Bourse went to buy from hold and upped its earnings forecast to 24 francs per share from 22.20 for 1997 and to 29.60 francs from 23.60 for 1998.
EIFB uprated the stock to overweight from underweight and revised 1997 earnings estimates to 25.20 francs from 22.80 and 28.70 from 25.70 for 1998.
Oddo marked it up to a buy from from overweight and forecast 1997 earnings of 32.20 francs from 24, and 35.80 from 27 for the following year.
SGE Delahaye held it at outperform and raised its forecasts, while Dupont Denant also maintained it at outperform, viewing the stock as undervalued.
Cheuvreux de Virieu, however, held its sell note, a "3" rating, and left its results forecasts unchanged.
